hints: Make the denominator real by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate $a+5i$.
Collect the real and imaginary terms separately to write the result as $x+iy$.
walkthrough:
Multiply numerator and denominator of $u = \dfrac{3 + 2\mathrm{i}}{a - 5\mathrm{i}}$ by the complex conjugate $(a + 5\mathrm{i})$:
$$u = \dfrac{(3 + 2\mathrm{i})(a + 5\mathrm{i})}{(a - 5\mathrm{i})(a + 5\mathrm{i})}$$

Expand the numerator and denominator:
$$\text{Numerator} = 3a + 15\mathrm{i} + 2a\mathrm{i} + 10\mathrm{i}^2 = (3a - 10) + (2a + 15)\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Denominator} = a^2 - 25\mathrm{i}^2 = a^2 + 25$$

Separate into real and imaginary parts to obtain Cartesian form:
$$u = \dfrac{3a - 10}{a^2 + 25} + \left(\dfrac{2a + 15}{a^2 + 25}\right)\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.Complex Algebra: Multiplies numerator and denominator by $a+5i$. Derives $\frac{3a-10}{a^2+25}+\frac{2a+15}{a^2+25}i$. Concludes with $u=\dfrac{3a-10}{a^2+25}+\dfrac{2a+15}{a^2+25}i$.

hints: Use the Cartesian form from part (a): its real and imaginary parts are $\dfrac{3a-10}{a^2+25}$ and $\dfrac{2a+15}{a^2+25}$.
Since $\arg u=\frac{\pi}{4}$, the imaginary and real parts are equal and positive.
Equate the two numerators and solve the resulting linear equation for $a$, checking the quadrant condition.
walkthrough:
Use the condition $\arg u = \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$:
In the first quadrant with argument $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, the tangent of the argument is $1$:
$$\tan(\arg u) = \dfrac{\operatorname{Im}(u)}{\operatorname{Re}(u)} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$$

Equate the numerator of the imaginary part to the numerator of the real part:
$$\dfrac{2a + 15}{a^2 + 25} = \dfrac{3a - 10}{a^2 + 25}$$
$$2a + 15 = 3a - 10$$

Verify that the real part is positive:
$$\operatorname{Re}(u) = \dfrac{3(25) - 10}{25^2 + 25} = \dfrac{65}{650} = \dfrac{1}{10} > 0$$
Conclude that $a = 25$.

ai_rubric.Complex Modulus and Argument: Identifies that the imaginary part divided by the real part is $1$; Derives $a=25$.
